cards.text: Jesus has been teaching in parables, like the one about a proud Pharisee and a humble tax collector (Luke 18:9-14). Now people are even bringing their babies to Him, so He can place His hands on them. BABIES, friend, and here they come!

cards.question: Jesus' disciples see people bringing their babies to Him. What do the disciples do?

cards.text: The disciples are acting like bouncers at a club: "Sorry, no babies tonight!" But Jesus calls the children to Him.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples not to hinder the little children, because the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

cards.text: Then Jesus goes further. He says there's a way the kingdom of God has to be received, or you never enter it at all.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little ___ will never enter it.

cards.text: Then a certain ruler comes to Jesus with a question, and friend, it's the BIGGEST question there is.

cards.question: What does the ruler ask Jesus?

answers.text: What must I do to inherit eternal life
Where will You go to teach next
Why do Your disciples not fast

cards.text: The ruler calls Jesus "Good Teacher." And Jesus stops right on that word: "Why do you call Me good?"

cards.question: Jesus tells the ruler that no one is good except God alone.

cards.text: Then Jesus points him to the commandments he already knows: do not commit adultery, murder, steal or bear false witness, and honor your father and mother.

cards.question: Jesus has listed the commandments. What does the ruler say about them?

answers.text: He has kept them all from his youth
He has broken a few of them lately
He still needs time to learn them all

cards.text: From his YOUTH, friend! I can't keep flour off my apron for five minutes, and this man says he's kept these since he was young.
Jesus hears this and tells the ruler he still lacks one thing.

cards.question: Jesus tells the ruler to sell everything he owns and give to the ___.
Jesus says the ruler will then have treasure in heaven. After that, what does Jesus invite the ruler to do?

cards.text: So there it is. The one thing he still lacks, and Jesus just told him exactly what to do about it.

cards.question: When the ruler hears what Jesus tells him, how does he take it?

answers.text: He runs off to sell it

cards.question: The ruler becomes very sad, because he is extremely ___.

cards.text: Jesus sees the man's sadness and says, "How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!"

cards.question: Jesus gives a picture of just how hard it is. What does He say is easier than a rich man entering the kingdom of God?

answers.text: A camel passing through the eye of a needle
A mountain being thrown into the sea
A city on a hill being hidden away

cards.text: A CAMEL, through the eye of a NEEDLE! Friend, I can't even get my chef's hat through my own oven door without a fight.

cards.question: The people who heard Jesus say this have a question of their own. What do they ask?

cards.text: Fair question! If it's that hard for the rich, they want to know who CAN make it, and Jesus has an answer.

cards.question: Jesus says what is impossible with man is possible with ___.

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, speaks up about himself and the others.

cards.question: What does Peter tell Jesus about himself and the other disciples?

answers.text: We have left all we had to follow You
We have kept every commandment too
We will sell all we have tomorrow

cards.text: Jesus answers, "Truly I tell you," and makes a promise to anyone who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who has left home or family for the sake of the kingdom of God will receive many times more in this age.
Jesus also makes a promise about the age to come. What does He say they will receive then?

cards.text: ETERNAL LIFE, the very thing the ruler asked Jesus about (Luke 18:18)! Many times more now and eternal life later, friend, and I thought getting pulled out of a junk drawer onto a whole cookie planet was a big upgrade.

findings.problem: The card's bouncer joke retells the disciples turning people away, which is Luke 18:15. The card only cites Luke 18:16, so the citation doesn't start at the first verse the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The statement says Jesus 'tells His disciples' not to hinder the children. Luke 18:16 says only that Jesus called the children to Him and said, 'Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them!' The text doesn't say who He is speaking to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This card only restates what card 14 and the answers to cards 15 and 16 already gave the baker, so it doesn't move the passage forward. It also cites Luke 18:22-23 but tells nothing from Luke 18:23.
Multiple choice is 4 of the stop's 6 choice cards (cards 2, 4, 8 and 11). Fill in the blank and true or false appear only once each.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question types open in a repeating cycle: multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, then multiple choice and true or false again (cards 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10). That reads as a formula, not a natural choice for each card.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Across 31 cards, only about four lines aim for a laugh: stop 1 cards 1, 3 and 13, and stop 2 cards 3 and 12. Several story cards are flat plot summaries with little of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 5, 7, 11 and 14, and stop 2 cards 7 and 9. Moments that can hold a real laugh go by without one, like the ruler calling Jesus 'Good Teacher', 'one thing' turning out to be selling everything, and Peter's 'Look'.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
